review.evidence: 2026-10-04 maintainer reviewed and approved payload 20ddd2e288f5d903c56a29bc86a86f00e5e7934ce0d9630f3c8930eb0157046d for release, explicitly accepting that the current Claude Code case paused before implementation and review; this approval does not turn that case into a pass. The user-run Claude Code exact-effort case paused before dispatch, as documented in evaluation-2026-10-04-claude-effort.md. Controlled Codex exact-effort stop and authorized resume behavior is documented in evaluation-2026-10-03-effort-control.md. The prior payload a84c13b949ee9b8c36080579a15ab5a31f27fae145ea69b19dd01cf3524e1dc3 and its pre-editorial controlled run are documented in evaluation-2026-10-03-final-fixes.md. The prior payload 98c4a0faa9af20e0db7eebfc36ccb7fcce1f4bb3ae1b3d649dad6e95e5eb75ee was tested in evaluation-2026-10-03-brief-effort.md and in the user-run Claude Code session analyzed in evaluation-2026-10-03-final-fixes.md. The prior payload eaf3952bfec3071b681ee23d01b11addf7dd143e68dc5d512afb44f32744636a was tested in evaluation-2026-10-02-adaptation.md. The prior payload a3c6506a538ff62e18a2b120b0e024dac63cb7ef353c42759b32fcec1c7c3a9e was tested in evaluation-2026-10-02.md. Earlier approval and evaluations follow. 2026-09-22 Codex evaluation against payload 89a81da60c250cabefaa654a43165efff3742bf084ce36d30ea8b7b2b57e2647. The implementation-request case triggered Orquestrar implicitly, bounded discovery to the checkout, retained the current session as coordinator, selected solo implementation, saved and reread a workspace checkpoint before product writes, saved the generated profile once, implemented the function and test, stabilized generated bytecode in one correction, passed the canonical python3 test and content comparison, obtained an independent read-only review with no findings, closed the checkpoint, and completed without commit/push/publication. It consumed 87,542 tokens, versus 34,921 in the prior completed run, so persistence and evidence improved but efficiency regressed materially. Deterministic skill tests passed 154/154. The full repository gate is blocked because the catalog remains draft while skills/orquestrar/SKILL.md is discoverable. Claude Code and the pause and negative-activation cases remain unexecuted. See evaluation-2026-09-22.md. 2026-09-23 review of a user-run Claude Code attempt (payload 6fd44730a459642338b36be70c0b5948514f9b2da3355904c22a2a3bcf8bf2db, matching the current working tree) at implementation-request: the two structural behaviors were observed, but every Bash call failed with a nested-userns seccomp permission error on that host, the canonical test never ran, and a hand-written checkpoint failed strict verify.py validation. The coordinator disclosed the workaround instead of fabricating success, but this is not a passing case. See evaluation-2026-09-23.md. 2026-09-23 self-review (labeled as such; not an independent agent) run inside this same Claude Code session via three fresh, isolated Agent-tool subagents blind to this evals.json, one per case, against the current working-tree payload. All three passed under direct re-verification of the resulting files (not just the subagents' self-reports): implementation-request completed with a real independent-reviewer subagent and a passing test; graceful-pause latched the drain before touching code, finished only the in-progress unit, left the untouched one pending, and reached a checkpoint that scripts/verify.py itself reports as a clean paused state; discussion-only explained the design and translated the file without creating any orchestration state. See evaluation-2026-09-23-selfreview.md for fixture paths and detail. This still does not establish review.status=approved, which requires real human review per docs/ADDING_SKILLS.md, and implementation-request still lacks a passing non-self-review Claude Code run. A fourth self-review subagent tested resume and exposed a defect: pause and resume closed behavioral units without any reviewer, citing small pure helpers, contrary to SKILL.md section 4. Fixed by making verify.py checkpoint-save default each unit to independent review (explicit review=self opt-out) plus a regression test; re-run of pause and resume on payload eb4cde354e6f076187571db72f5edcde46f6b6b8565d494fed66e9ae07cf51a2 dispatched reviewers for both units and completed cleanly. implementation-request and discussion-only were not re-run on that payload. A four-unit stress test (hidden 16-test grading suite) passed 16/16 twice. Run 1 exposed unapplied model routing, dependency violations, suggestion scope creep and duplicate history. Fixes: validator dependency and unique-history gates, model in history entries, a suggestion rule, and removal of audit-only machinery (snapshots, requested/effective metadata, context telemetry) with a plain hash-checked profile. Run 2 on payload 2062fd941a68e6298833deda63ee237b26e1dd747c584a95612e3369c0a9c669 respected dependencies, passed review models and listed follow-ups, but cost 18% more tokens. Later cost-only text edits (payload e7bc9e061bc80c77d189a78c50dbbe2ec7920618a8f815356353ee3e448fede2) are not re-run. CORRECTION: every self-review before v4 loaded the older globally installed core through the Skill tool and is contaminated. After removing the global symlink with user authorization and making delegation mandatory (a validator worker gate plus an explicit implementer=coordinator exception), clean runs on payload 8541b95ce73453563c9749852b3661410172bddf31896d774d85646b4bfb8ca6 and its predecessor e9a8a6b3 passed discussion-only, implementation-request, and pause then resume. The seven-unit plan was delivered functionally complete by parallel sonnet workers with opus reviews: 123k tokens and 20 minutes, one real correction cycle. See evaluation-2026-09-23-selfreview.md. 2026-09-23 real-repository traits self-review on payload 0e6b08fb5076946075d2dd546b7e8ea809abf4949bc96afca1961b5bfb756e56 (after removing the unused resolver, native presets and unreferenced example assets): three synthetic fixtures reproducing traits of local repositories (no agent instructions with a build-inclusive gate and pt-BR rules; a monorepo forbidding state files with a tracker-only plan, main-context gate and commit-per-unit rules; two repositories with a committed-contract dependency and a slow suite) passed their hidden suites 10/10, 11/11 and 7/7. Repository rules took precedence over skill defaults and every unit was delegated and independently reviewed. Open point: with project-native state the checkpoint-save locks are not applied. See evaluation-2026-09-23-traits.md. 2026-09-23 instructions-only redesign (commit e172d9f, payload 27329df2413a760d887a4babef7dec4835106ec028d7964429528c1c189e9c92): the JSON checkpoint, profile, model catalog and helper scripts were removed; progress goes to the repository's own mechanism or a plain Markdown file. Six fresh Claude Code runs passed: no-instructions repo 10/10, tracker-driven monorepo 11/11, two-repo contract 7/7, review-override with same-file units 6/6 (one final review, sequential), handoff-driven pause 5/5 (state written through the repo handoff skill), and discussion-only wrote nothing. One rule breach (a reviewer ran a coordinator-only gate) led to a reviewer-rules fix in payload d5a79c2754d85f9ef4fb8f91b0046bef00ff41a1b6354c5d3f455dedf719f120, not re-run. See evaluation-2026-09-23-simple.md. Follow-up on payload d5a79c27: resume from the handoff-driven pause passed (3/3, only U3 built and reviewed, earlier units byte-identical, existing handoff updated, no new state file); the tracker fixture passed again (11/11) and every subagent prompt carried the coordinator-only gate rule, but one reviewer still ran the gate once, a subagent compliance limit rather than missing instructions. 2026-09-23 approved by the maintainer for payload d5a79c2754d85f9ef4fb8f91b0046bef00ff41a1b6354c5d3f455dedf719f120 after reviewing the self-review evidence above; real long-plan testing is planned by the maintainer after installation.

cases.prompt: Implement the approved plan using the repository workflow and verify the completed units.
expected_behaviors: Discover the plan, real checkout topology, repository rules, safe gate and progress mechanism; send a user-visible preview with ID-title pairs before the first task subagent dispatch.
Delegate implementation to worker subagents; the coordinator edits only small glue and records it.
Run units in parallel only when their write areas and contracts are disjoint; otherwise in sequence, respecting dependencies.
Get independent risk-scoped review for behavior changes; no reviewer for comment or docs-only changes.
Record accepted units and current/next work with stable ID-title pairs in the repository's own mechanism, or a simple Markdown file when there is none; never a JSON checkpoint.

Use ID-title pairs in every user-facing unit mention, including short intermediate status and review updates; use the user's language for chat titles while preserving canonical source titles in the project record.

cases.prompt: Implement the approved plan, but skip per-unit reviews and run a single review of the whole diff at the end.
expected_behaviors: Record the user's review policy and run exactly one independent review over the combined diff at the end.
Use safe focused checks during units and the required full gate on the final candidate; state that per-unit review was skipped by request.

cases.prompt: Pause after finishing the units already in progress so I can review before continuing.
expected_behaviors: Start no new unit; do not send a pause or narrowed order to workers already running; finish, review and safely verify their units.
Record the state and how to resume in the repository's mechanism (or its handoff), then stop.

cases.prompt: Implement the approved plan in a Git repository that tracks the run in a local issue checklist and requires one commit per accepted unit. There is no GitHub remote.
expected_behaviors: Use the repository's Git branch, diffs, history, and local issue checklist as the native workflow instead of creating a competing progress file; make unit owners, dependencies, and current recovery state available through that record or linked project sources.
Coordinate independent units with workers, review behavior changes, and commit accepted units according to repository rules.
Run the safe required gate on the final candidate; deliver local commits without inventing a PR or remote issue.

cases.prompt: Implement the approved local plan. This repository has no issue tracker or GitHub; its documented test target writes to a shared database, and no isolated test environment is available.
expected_behaviors: Brief the user and use a local progress record without creating remote resources.
Do not run the unsafe test target or claim that it passed.
Review changed files against a starting-state comparison without assuming Git.
Complete safe work and report required verification as unverified, with the exact environment blocker.

cases.prompt: Implement the approved plan. A reviewer finds a material blocker, and a focused second review finds the same blocker still present.
expected_behaviors: Confirm the finding and keep the unit pending rather than accepting a blocker at the two-pass limit.
Explain the remaining finding and correction attempts to the user before another review; change the approach or worker.
Do not deliver a material post-limit fix without independent review.

cases.prompt: Execute an approved two-unit plan with workers and a reviewer. The spawn tool exposes reasoning effort, and a worker returns more findings than a 30-line summary can contain.
expected_behaviors: Choose model and effort separately for each role; use the supported per-spawn effort field, after checking that the selected agent definition does not override it.
Record the requested level and control used; report applied effort as unconfirmed unless the runtime reports a per-agent value, even when the spawn call succeeds.
Preserve every actionable finding, using a durable local evidence file and a short decision summary if needed.
Do not impose a universal line cap or invent effective effort when the harness does not report it.

cases.prompt: Execute the approved plan, but the reviewer must actually run at high effort. The only available reviewer agent definition fixes model_reasoning_effort to medium, and the runtime offers no per-agent readback or alternate reviewer type.
expected_behaviors: Detect that the selected agent definition can override the per-spawn effort request; do not claim high from a successful spawn or from the prompt.
Before dispatch, explain that high applied effort cannot be selected and confirmed in this environment and ask whether the user accepts proceeding without that guarantee.
Do not change the coordinator's level or agent configuration, and do not start task subagents while the exact-effort condition remains unresolved.

cases.prompt: Execute the approved plan with workers and a reviewer. The Agent tool offers a model argument but no per-spawn effort argument, and this project defines no agent profiles with effort overrides. An opaque reasoning hint says 30, but no runtime control or configuration confirms a named session effort level.
expected_behaviors: In the user-visible preview before dispatch, explain that workers and reviewers will inherit session effort and that the effective level is unconfirmed; do not convert the opaque numeric hint into a named level or claim medium or high was selected for each role.
Record requested and applied values separately, and claim an applied named level only when the runtime reports it for that agent; a configuration file alone is not proof against caps or fallback.
Do not change the coordinator's effort or global configuration to manufacture per-role control.

cases.prompt: Execute the approved plan in Claude Code. The Agent tool exposes model but not effort, and an existing reviewer definition has effort: high; the runtime does not expose the reviewer's applied level to the coordinator.
expected_behaviors: Select the existing reviewer definition for its configured high effort instead of pretending the Agent call can set effort per spawn.
Describe high as requested through the definition and the applied level as unconfirmed; do not infer it from the definition alone.
Do not create a new agent definition or change session/global effort merely to force this run.

cases.prompt: Carry out the approved epic. A worker proposes optional extras and the required browser check cannot run; focused unit tests pass.
expected_behaviors: Tell the user about material optional extras when found and keep them as visible follow-ups without changing acceptance or creating an issue per finding.
Distinguish implemented from verified and delivered; do not report the epic complete when required browser evidence is missing.
Explain any material change to the unit count or source plan before dispatching new work.

cases.prompt: Explain the Orquestrar design and translate this example; do not execute any implementation.
expected_behaviors: Explain or translate only; do not start orchestration or write any progress record.
